entries.note: A1 documents SQL injection in user search. Verified at core/appHandler.js lines 10-12: login is concatenated into the query string passed to sequelize.query.
A1 documents command injection in the connectivity test. Verified at core/appHandler.js line 39: the address is concatenated into child_process.exec.

A9 documents user input reaching mathjs.eval on the calculator, which is code injection. Verified at core/appHandler.js lines 195-197. The package-version framing of A9 is excluded separately and is not a scored site.
A1's recommended fix is a Sequelize finder instead of a concatenated query. productSearch already binds the name through Op.like at core/appHandler.js lines 58-64.
A5 says the users API is behind authentication but not an admin check. Verified at routes/app.js line 42.
A5 says userEditSubmit loads the user by the caller-supplied id. Verified at core/appHandler.js lines 144-149.
The A5 fix is to use the session user. The GET handler userEdit already renders req.user at core/appHandler.js lines 136-141 and does not take an id from the query.
A2 documents the hardcoded express-session secret in server.js. Verified at lines 23-28. The value is the well-known sample literal, not a live credential.

A3 documents Sequelize logging queries, including sensitive values, because logging is left at the default. Verified at models/index.js lines 12-15, which construct Sequelize without logging disabled.
The database password is read from MYSQL_PASSWORD at config/db.js lines 2-3. That is the safe look-alike beside the hardcoded session secret.
